newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada court to hear pregnant glue-sniffer case.
newsitem.headline: Canada court to hear pregnant glue-sniffer case.

text.p: The Canadian Supreme Court agreed on Friday to consider whether the government can force a pregnant glue-sniffer into treatment to protect the health of her fetus, a case with implications for abortion rights.
The Manitoba Court of Appeals, citing an earlier Supreme Court decision that a fetus is not a person, had ordered that the woman be allowed to leave an addiction-treatment program.
The Winnipeg Child and Family Services agency sought to appeal.
The Supreme Court gave no reasons for its decision hear the case. If it had refused to hear the appeal, the previous judgment freeing the woman would have automatically stood.
The Winnipeg agency appealed because two of the woman's three other children were born with a chemical addiction and were developmentally handicapped, a court summary said.
A lower court had ordered the woman, in her early 20s, into an addiction treatment program on August 6 but the appeals court reversed this on September 12. Her baby is due in December.
Canada has been without an abortion law since 1988, when the Supreme Court struck down provisions of the criminal code on the grounds that it violated the "liberty and security of the person."
